A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniSch, and their supplied text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. Both end with references on page 17 and contain no appendices or embedded attachments, despite referring to appendices. Main-text comparison is reliable, but appendix-dependent implementation details and results are unavailable.

before.justification: v1 reports original schematic-understanding experiments, prompting ablations, and agentic evaluations in Tables 2–4 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v4 reports original model evaluations, controlled ablations, human-reference results, and agentic comparisons in Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The reported alignment algorithm changes: v1 describes separate semantic and structure-only matching protocols, whereas v4 Section 3.5 specifies weighted symbol/pin scores combining attributes with positional or structural information. Hierarchical bipartite matching remains. Expanded descriptions of the rendering and ReAct frameworks do not establish additional architectural changes.

E1.justification: The same 1,854-schematic OmniSch corpus and schematic-understanding tasks remain. v4 adds an explicitly evaluated low-resolution input condition, represented by the Real Low R. rows in Table 2. Real, synthesized, and symbol-text-removed inputs were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The few-shot comparison expands from GPT-5.2 alone to nine LMMs. Table 2 also adds a Human Engineer reference and replaces Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B with Qwen3.5-122B-A10B. Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B remains in the agentic comparison, whose model membership is retained. The newly mentioned SFT model has no separately identifiable result row.

E3.justification: v4 revises graph alignment and expands reported evaluation to separate attribute-based and IoU-based detection matching, net detection F1, 1-GED, and pass rate. It adds low-resolution and broader few-shot controls while retaining the 80/10/10 split. Agentic guidance changes from detector-output wording to GT BBox labeling, although the caption still says detector-assisted; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds resolution sensitivity testing and extends few-shot ablations across models. v1's few-shot-plus-explicit-instruction condition is no longer shown. Its Figure 5 analyses of exploration direction, crop-area distributions, and tracing accuracy versus search steps are also absent from the supplied v4; the new Figures 5–6 illustrate inputs and workflow instead.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark scores. Changing agentic improvement values from absolute differences to relative percentages does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 extensively replaces scores and adds results. Gemini 3.1 Pro's Real Kendall's tau changes from 0.6438 to 0.0432. Gemini 2.5 Flash's symbol-detection response to text removal reverses: 0.4516 to 0.3077 in v1, versus 0.5622 to 0.7241 in v4. Several agentic cells also change. Revised evaluation rules prevent interpreting these as demonstrated same-protocol performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v4 introduces task-specific mathematical definitions for weighted symbol and pin similarity in Equations 1–2, replacing v1's prose matching rules and changing how positional or structural information enters scoring. This is a localized change to evaluation mathematics; neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: a comprehensive real-world schematic benchmark, evaluation of grounding and graph reasoning, substantial LMM weaknesses, and benefits from tool-augmented visual search. Additional experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v4 emphasizes the human–model gap and the distinction between semantic recognition and precise localization, replacing v1's account of strong Gemini 3.1 end-to-end spatial reasoning. It adds a precision–recall explanation for text-removal gains and discusses resolution sensitivity. Detailed explanations concerning procedural prompting mismatch, crop concentration, and Qwen's empty-schema failures are no longer included.

D1.justification: v4 adds main-text descriptions of OCR-to-instance grounding and the query-and-crop agentic workflow, depicts visual working memory, and supplies DPI labels and a project-page address. These expand documentation, but matching weights, detailed training settings, and human-evaluation procedures remain unspecified in the supplied material. The address alone does not establish code or data availability.

R1.justification: v4 adds the Qwen technical report and a dedicated Ultralytics YOLO11 reference. Section 3.5 newly states that no standardized LMM netlist-graph matching protocol exists. The main related-work discussion and Table 1 retain their previous research positioning.

P1.justification: The evaluation and experimental narrative is extensively rewritten. Matching becomes Section 3.5, another Evaluation Criteria subsection appears as Section 3.6, and separate results and seven numbered findings become a combined capability- and study-based discussion. The author list expands and the placeholder running title is corrected.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially redesigned with more conditions and metric columns, incorporating expanded prompting results. The agentic table is reordered and reformatted with model sizes and percentage differences. v1's three-panel behavioral-analysis figure disappears, while v4 adds schematic-variation and agentic-workflow figures. Figures 1–4 remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicit matching equations, separate localization scores, a human reference, and broader ablations improve evaluation coverage and interpretability. However, v4 removes quantitative agent-behavior diagnostics and leaves important new evaluation details unresolved. It also introduces contradictory summaries: Section 4.2 calls 27.44% the best LMM net-detection F1, although Table 2 reports 42.37% for Qwen3.5. Together with unclear detector-versus-ground-truth guidance and unavailable appendices, these tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
